subject: Medicore — LLM processing boundaries, derivative rights & subprocessor routing
messages:
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medicore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@medicore.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Draft DPA questions — LLM training & subprocessors

Hi Karthik,

Thanks for sending over the draft DPA. A few items the Medicore legal/ops team flagged that we need to resolve before procurement can progress:

- No-training / model improvement: the current clause is vague about whether Redwood will use any derived outputs (responses, embeddings, prompts) to improve models. We need an explicit operational commitment (no-training) for Medicore data unless we opt-in.
- Prompt/response ownership: we need assurance that outputs generated for our tenants are not treated as Redwood IP or used in ways that would expose our confidential prompts.
- Subprocessor inventory & routing: please provide the current subprocessor list and confirm where our data will be processed (US/ EU onshore routing options). Medicore requires an inventory CSV and an evidence pack for one-off audits.
- Cross-border transfers: if any processing occurs outside the EU for EU-resident data, we need clarity on safeguards and Data Transfer Mechanisms.

I've attached the latest Medicore_DPA_Draft_v3.pdf with inline comments. Can you please confirm which items Redwood can commit to as-is and which will require redlines? If helpful, propose a short set of contract language we can include that meets our security requirements.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call next week.

— Elena
Elena Torres
VP, Legal Operations
Medicore Health

Attachments: Medicore_DPA_Draft_v3.pdf
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medicore.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Fri, 12 Sep 2025 11:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA questions — LLM training & subprocessors

Hi Elena — thanks for the thorough notes and the draft. Appreciated.

High-level answers up front:
- No-training: Redwood can commit to a contractual No‑Model‑Improvement covenant for Medicore production tenant traffic (we call this the "no-training" toggle). We will include explicit language that customers' production prompt/response interactions will not be used for model updates or retraining.
- Prompt/response ownership: Redwood will not claim ownership of customer prompts or outputs. We can include a clause that grants Medicore exclusive rights to outputs generated from your tenant data and prohibits Redwood from exploiting them outside support/ops.
- Subprocessors: attaching our current subprocessor_inventory.csv. We operate a mix of cloud infra and specialized inference partners; some services (e.g., telemetry analytics) are handled by third parties. We can offer onshore routing and KMS options for EU-resident data as part of the Dedicated/Private offering.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment call (30m) – include Product/Legal/Infra — suggest Tue 9/16 or Wed 9/17.
2) We will produce an evidence pack (operational runbook + attestation) demonstrating no-training enforcement and export controls by 9/18.
3) Draft proposed contract text for the clauses you flagged and share redlines by EOD 9/15.

I've looped in David (infra) and Marissa (legal solutions) to provide the operational proof and the evidence template we typically use.

Best,
Karthik
Head of Business, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-evidence-template.docx
From: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medicore.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Sep 2025 10:28:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA questions — LLM training & subprocessors

Elena — quick technical note from infra/ops:

- Operationalizing No‑Training: We implement a tenant-level flag that prevents telemetry and interaction payloads from entering any training/replication pipelines. The flag is enforced at the routing layer and verified in batch jobs; we log enforcement events to an auditable stream.
- Evidence: attached is the subprocessor_inventory.csv and a one-page proof-of-enforcement checklist (we'll populate the evidence pack).
- Onshore routing & KMS: For EU-resident data we can route inference and short-lived KV cache to EU regions and use customer-managed KMS for encryption-at-rest. Full on-prem keys (HSM) are available under Redwood Private.
- Exportability & deletions: We can implement customer-initiated deletion hooks and provide export of tenant transcripts. For long-term retention policies we propose a configurable TTL; immediate deletion requests will be acknowledged in our audit logs and retained only for the minimum time required for operational reconciliation.

Open items for legal: SLAs around proof delivery (how quickly does Medicore need the pack?), and whether Medicore requires escrow/third-party verification.

— David
David Kim
Director, Platform Reliability
Redwood Inference

Attachments: subprocessor_inventory.csv
From: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medicore.com>
To: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
Cc: Legal Team <legal@medicore.com>, Raj Patel <raj.patel@medicore.com>
Date: Wed, 17 Sep 2025 08:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA questions — LLM training & subprocessors

Thanks Karthik and David — this helps. A couple of clarifying asks from Medicore Legal:

1) We need proposed contract language for the no-training promise that is narrowly tailored and includes remedies (audit rights or third-party attestation). Suggested starter text from our counsel: "Provider warrants that it will not use customer data, prompts, or outputs to train, tune, or otherwise improve models except with Customer's prior written consent. Provider will provide evidence of non‑use upon Customer request within 10 business days, and shall allow a one‑time third‑party attestation per 12‑month period."

2) For cross-border transfer language, we prefer standard SCCs + onshore routing; please confirm whether Redwood will accept SCCs for transfers and include a registry of subprocessors subject to onshore-only processing.

3) Evidence pack: Medicore requires the evidence pack delivered as a single zipped artifact with (a) enforcement logs (redacted), (b) subprocessor attestations, (c) config snapshots demonstrating tenant flag, and (d) KMS key residency confirmation. Can Redwood commit to those components?

We also have an internal procurement timeline: final contract by 9/30 to meet our Q4 launch.

Elena

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik.iyer@redwoodinference.com>
To: Elena Torres <elena.torres@medicore.com>
Cc: David Kim <david.kim@redwoodinference.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwoodinference.com>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com>
Date: Thu, 18 Sep 2025 15:32:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Draft DPA questions — LLM training & subprocessors

Elena — quick summary and commitments so Medicore procurement has a clear record:

Agreed / Redwood commitments:
- Contract text: Redwood will accept the "no-training" clause in the form you suggested with a minor edit to clarify that the remedy is limited to evidence provision and a right to a third-party attestation (we will propose specific language in redlines by 9/15 — full redline now attached in HubSpot link).
- Evidence pack: Redwood commits to deliver a zipped evidence artifact (a–d as listed) by 2025-09-18. If Medicore needs escrow verification we can discuss scope and cost separately.
- SCCs & transfers: Redwood accepts SCCs for EU transfers and will include an annotated subprocessor registry indicating which subprocessors are eligible for onshore-only processing.
- Operational controls: tenant-level no-training flag, auditable enforcement logs, and customer-managed KMS are available as described.

Open items / asks from Medicore:
- Confirmation that a single third-party attestation per 12 months is acceptable (we included the right in the contract but want to confirm the frequency).
- Procurement timeline confirmation (target final contract 9/30).

Next steps:
1) Deliver evidence pack (zip) by end of day 9/18 — David and Marissa will own delivery.
2) Redwood legal to upload redline DPA to the shared Drive and HubSpot record by 9/15 (link: https://hubspot.com/deals/MDCR-2025-045).
3) Schedule a 30m call if Medicore wants to discuss attestation scope — propose Mon 9/22 10am PT.

I'll follow up once the evidence artifact is uploaded. Thanks everyone for the quick turn.

— Karthik
Head of Business, North America
Redwood Inference

Attachments (referenced): redwood-evidence-template.docx, subprocessor_inventory.csv
